prose	pages	site/pages/about.html	The 1984 ward map took months of evenings this way. The same method has since been applied to Republic of Ireland electoral divisions, and it is the work we most need help with. prose	pages	site/pages/about.html	The maps are the means, not the end. Civgraph exists so that the data attached to Irish places can be compared across time by anyone who wants to, and not only by people who have GIS software and the patience to reconcile forty years of boundary changes before they can start.
prose	pages	site/pages/about.html	The obstacle to using any of it together is that the boundaries move. Census geographies change, wards and constituencies are redrawn every ten to fifteen years, and almost nothing can be compared like-for-like across decades unless you know precisely which boundaries were in force when. That's the gap Civgraph fills.
